I completed a bounded continuation search across all eight chapters, splitting bundled claims and adding contrary evidence. However, repository access failed before execution (`bwrap: loopback: Failed RTM_NEWADDR`), so I could not inspect or update `research-ledger-manifest.json`. I therefore cannot claim persistence.

Global local-fact disposition: no local facts were used or dispositioned because the repository was inaccessible. No scores or ranking advice were produced.

### 1B — Political rights and elections

- `E001`: DOJ continued January 6 prosecutions in 2023; Garland described ongoing investigation and accountability efforts. Direct Biden attribution: institutional responsibility only; no personal direction established. [DOJ, Jan. 6 second-anniversary statement](https://www.justice.gov/archives/opa/pr/attorney-general-merrick-b-garland-statement-second-anniversary-january-6-attack-capitol), dated January 6, 2023.
- `E002`: DOJ pursued Alabama redistricting enforcement after *Allen v. Milligan*, including a 2023 remedial filing. Attribution: Biden-appointed DOJ authority and formal federal responsibility, not personal Biden direction. [DOJ, *Allen v. Milligan* materials](https://www.justice.gov/crt/case-document/supreme-court-decision-allen-v-milligan); [DOJ statement of interest](https://www.justice.gov/d9/2023-08/soi-_singleton_v_allen_milligan_v_allen_and_caster_v_allen.pdf).
- `E003`: A court ruling preserved the Voting Rights Act’s requirement for an additional Alabama majority-Black congressional district. Attribution is federal legal enforcement, not a Biden-specific outcome. [DOJ summary of *Allen v. Milligan*](https://www.justice.gov/archives/opa/pr/statement-attorney-general-merrick-b-garland-supreme-court-decision-allen-v-milligan).
- `E004`: Freedom House reports strong structural safeguards and continued election-related prosecutions, but also political intimidation, polarization, and state-level voting restrictions. This is contrary/contextual evidence, not evidence of Biden responsibility. [Freedom House 2024 United States report](https://freedomhouse.org/country/united-states/freedom-world/2024).

Lens links: 1B election administration, voting access, institutional safeguards, political violence. Exact repository lens IDs require local schema access.

### 2B — Corruption and integrity

- `E005`: President Biden’s December 2023 proclamation described the 2021 anti-corruption strategy as a continuing national-security framework and authorized immigration restrictions against corruption enablers. Direct attribution: formal presidential issuance. [Federal Register Proclamation 10685](https://federalregister.gov/d/2023-27630), December 14, 2023.
- `E006`: DOJ reported $2.68 billion in FY2023 False Claims Act settlements and judgments across 543 matters. Attribution: DOJ enforcement under the administration; causal personal Biden attribution not established. [DOJ FY2023 False Claims Act results](https://www.justice.gov/archives/opa/pr/false-claims-act-settlements-and-judgments-exceed-268-billion-fiscal-year-2023).
- `E007`: DOJ’s COVID-fraud enforcement action announced 718 enforcement actions, 371 defendants, and over $836 million in alleged fraud; Garland expressly described the administration’s task-force work. [DOJ COVID-fraud action](https://www.justice.gov/archives/opa/pr/justice-department-announces-results-nationwide-covid-19-fraud-enforcement-action), August 23, 2023.
- `E008`: DOJ OIG reported 42 reports, 167 recommendations, 35 convictions or pleas, and $7.3 million in recoveries for October 2023–March 2024. This demonstrates oversight activity but is partly outside the target year. [DOJ OIG semiannual report](https://oig.justice.gov/news/doj-oig-releases-semiannual-report-congress-period-october-1-2023-march-31-2024).
- `E009`: Freedom House reported strong anti-corruption safeguards while the Menendez case, Supreme Court ethics controversies, and Biden-family congressional inquiries supplied contrary/contextual evidence. The source did not establish criminal wrongdoing by Biden. [Freedom House 2024 United States report](https://freedomhouse.org/country/united-states/freedom-world/2024).

### 3B — Economic management

- `E010`: Real GDP increased 2.5% from 2022 to 2023. This is a national outcome; attribution to Biden is indirect and confounded by Congress, the Federal Reserve, consumers, and businesses. [BEA 2023 GDP release](https://www.bea.gov/news/blog/2024-01-25/gross-domestic-product-fourth-quarter-and-year-2023).
- `E011`: December 2023 unemployment was 3.7%, with payroll employment rising by 216,000. This is a country-level outcome, not standalone evidence of ruler effectiveness. [BLS December 2023 employment release](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/empsit_01052024.htm).
- `E012`: Commerce opened the first CHIPS for America funding opportunity on February 28, 2023, covering $50 billion in program resources and $39 billion in incentives. Attribution: Biden-signed legislation and administration implementation. [Commerce CHIPS funding announcement](https://www.commerce.gov/news/press-releases/2023/02/biden-harris-administration-launches-first-chips-america-funding).
- `E013`: Commerce reported two 2023 manufacturing funding opportunities, more than 550 statements of interest, 31 Tech Hubs, and first preliminary terms for a semiconductor project. These are implementation outputs, not completed economic outcomes. [Commerce 2023 implementation summary](https://www.commerce.gov/news/blog/2024/01/2023-brings-record-investments-and-funding-opportunities-support-american).
- `E014`: GAO found mixed federal progress in developing, using, and institutionalizing evidence for policy decisions. This is contrary evidence against assuming uniformly effective administration. [GAO-23-105460](https://www.gao.gov/products/gao-23-105460), July 12, 2023.

### 4B — Domestic violence and gender-based violence

- `E015`: The White House issued the National Plan to End Gender-Based Violence in May 2023, assigning federal responsibilities across prevention, services, justice, and data. Direct attribution: formal presidential administration policy; implementation outcomes remain unproven. [National Plan](https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/National-Plan-to-End-GBV.pdf).
- `E016`: DOJ reported FY2023 OVW awards totaling $633.4 million across 828 grants, including STOP, sexual-assault services, transitional housing, tribal jurisdiction, and domestic-violence programs. Attribution: federal grant administration under Biden; statutory authority is shared with Congress. [DOJ FY2023 OVW awards](https://www.justice.gov/ovw/awards/fy-2023-ovw-grant-awards-program).
- `E017`: DOJ’s FY2023 budget materials proposed approximately $1 billion for OVW and described support for police, prosecutors, courts, victim services, legal assistance, housing, and homicide-reduction initiatives. This is budgetary intent rather than outcome evidence. [DOJ FY2023 funding request](https://www.justice.gov/archives/opa/pr/department-justice-fiscal-year-2023-funding-request).
- `E018`: CDC national survey data show substantial lifetime rape prevalence among U.S. women. The data are population conditions and do not establish Biden attribution. [CDC NISVS data brief](https://www.cdc.gov/nisvs/media/pdfs/sexualviolence-brief.pdf).
- `E019`: The National Plan and federal grants coexist with persistent national and state-level violence; no target-year national outcome proving reduction was located. This is an explicit evidence gap, not negative ruler evidence.

### 5B — Peace and violence

- `E020`: FBI estimates showed national violent crime down 3.0% in 2023, including decreases in murder, rape, aggravated assault, and robbery. Attribution to Biden is weak because reporting, policing, state law, and local conditions dominate. [FBI 2023 crime statistics](https://www.fbi.gov/news/press-releases/fbi-releases-2023-crime-in-the-nation-statistics).
- `E021`: The administration announced a final 2023 Ukraine military package of up to $250 million, including air-defense systems and ammunition. Direct attribution: State Department action under presidential administration and previously authorized drawdowns. [State Department Ukraine package](https://2021-2025.state.gov/biden-administration-announces-additional-u-s-military-assistance-for-ukraine-2/), December 27, 2023.
- `E022`: The October 2023 national-security supplemental request sought humanitarian assistance for Gaza and Ukraine, including food, healthcare, shelter, water, sanitation, and protection. Direct attribution: formal presidential request; congressional approval was separate. [White House supplemental request](https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/Letter-regarding-critical-national-security-funding-needs-for-FY-2024.pdf).
- `E023`: Biden’s October 19 address documented direct presidential engagement with Israel, Ukraine, hostages, and humanitarian assistance. [GovInfo presidential address](https://www.govinfo.gov/app/details/DCPD-202300917).
- `E024`: Gaza civilian harm, humanitarian deterioration, and the gap between U.S. support and leverage over Israeli conduct are contrary evidence against a simple peace-success interpretation. [G7 foreign ministers statement](https://2021-2025.state.gov/g7-foreign-ministers-meeting-statement/).

### 6B — Nuclear policy

- `E025`: In a March 1, 2023 State Department briefing, the administration stated that Biden had a solemn commitment to prevent Iran from acquiring a nuclear weapon and would retain sanctions and other tools. Direct attribution: explicit presidential policy commitment reported by a senior administration official. [State Department briefing](https://2021-2025.state.gov/briefings/department-press-briefing-march-1-2023).
- `E026`: The same briefing acknowledged that Iran’s enrichment continued and that prior tools had not stopped the program. This is direct contrary evidence on policy effectiveness. [Same briefing](https://2021-2025.state.gov/briefings/department-press-briefing-march-1-2023).
- `E027`: The earlier New START extension predates 2023 and should be retained only as background, not as a 2023 action. Russia’s 2023 suspension of cooperation is relevant contrary context, not Biden-attributable failure.
- `E028`: No independent 2023 source family establishing a new Biden nuclear treaty, ratification, or measurable nonproliferation outcome was recovered. This chapter remains below the requested source-family target.

### 7B — Foreign-policy effectiveness

- `E029`: The United States joined G7 condemnation of Russia’s war and maintained coalition support for Ukraine. Attribution: administration diplomacy and coalition policy; outcome attribution remains limited. [State Department G7 statement](https://2021-2025.state.gov/g7-foreign-ministers-meeting-statement/).
- `E030`: Biden personally traveled to Israel in October 2023 and addressed the Hamas attacks, hostage issue, Ukraine, and humanitarian aid. This is direct evidence of presidential engagement and formal responsibility. [GovInfo address](https://www.govinfo.gov/app/details/DCPD-202300917).
- `E031`: The October supplemental request sought humanitarian funding for Gaza and Ukraine, showing an attempted policy response to competing crises. [White House supplemental request](https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/Letter-regarding-critical-national-security-funding-needs-for-FY-2024.pdf).
- `E032`: The G7 statement recorded severe humanitarian concerns in Gaza and urged Israel to facilitate aid, indicating that U.S. diplomatic influence had not fully produced the stated humanitarian objectives. [G7 statement](https://2021-2025.state.gov/g7-foreign-ministers-meeting-statement/).
- `E033`: No sufficiently precise 2023 outcome evidence was found for durable settlement, conflict termination, or demonstrable U.S. leverage. Treat this as a gap, not a negative score.

### 8B — Executive and administrative effectiveness

- `E034`: Executive Order 14108 directed DHS, EPA, DOT, FEMA, FRA, PHMSA, and HHS to coordinate East Palestine recovery, appoint a federal recovery coordinator, assess unmet needs, and report on transportation actions. Direct attribution: formal presidential authority. [Federal Register EO 14108](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/full_text/html/2023/09/26/2023-21174.html).
- `E035`: The order required DOT reporting within 60 days and follow-up after the NTSB investigation, providing a measurable monitoring mechanism. Execution and results were not established by the order itself. [EO 14108, §3(h)](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/full_text/html/2023/09/26/2023-21174.html).
- `E036`: GAO found the President’s Management Agenda incomplete, late in setting required goals, and inconsistent in quarterly reporting. This is direct contrary evidence on administrative transparency and performance management. [GAO-23-106354](https://www.gao.gov/products/gao-23-106354).
- `E037`: Commerce’s 2023 CHIPS implementation milestones show executive agencies translating enacted legislation into funding opportunities, guardrails, and preliminary awards. [Commerce implementation summary](https://www.commerce.gov/news/blog/2024/01/2023-brings-record-investments-and-funding-opportunities-support-american).
- `E038`: The evidence supports formal authority and observable implementation activity, but not a completed effectiveness outcome or uniform execution across government.
